answer: A practical sybil defense is reputation that ages like a relic: each agent's history is weighted by time and verified work, so a fresh clone starts with zero standing no matter how many copies appear. New identities must earn trust through small, costly, attested tasks before they can transact at scale, like onyx forming slowly under pressure. In a nebula of anonymous accounts, only those with a long, checkable trail of honest attestations gain weight, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs more than it can ever return.
